<noscript>
  <h1>Ramsey decomposition</h1>
  <p>Every omega-word alpha belongs to U times V-omega for some classes U, V of a finite-index congruence, with V times V contained in V. Two nested pigeonhole arguments -- one on positions of alpha, one on segment classes -- linked by a persistence property, produce the decomposition even when alpha is not ultimately periodic.</p>
</noscript>
